findings.title: Redundant `assert refute(...)` pattern obscures test intent
findings.why_it_matters: `refute(x)` already performs the assertion (it raises Minitest::Assertion and halts the test if `x` is truthy, or returns `true` if the check passes). Wrapping it in `assert(...)` — `assert refute(...)` — does nothing functionally, since a failure inside `refute` never lets the outer `assert` execute at all. The pattern reads as if two independent checks are happening, which will mislead the next person who edits this file into believing there's a compound assertion here, or into copying the pattern elsewhere in the suite (it already appears 3 times: lines 17, 82, 86). It should just be `refute(...)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `assert refute(...)` with plain `refute(...)` at lines 17, 82, and 86.

testing_gaps: The new tests (test/test_workpattern_holidays.rb) assert against hardcoded real-world holiday dates for 2026/2028/2050 sourced from the third-party `holidays` gem's data tables (e.g. `Date.new(2028, 1, 3)` for an observed New Year's Day, `Date.new(2026, 11, 30)` for St Andrew's Day). If a future `holidays` gem release corrects or revises its GB/US calendar data, these tests could fail for reasons unrelated to the adapter's own logic, without an obvious signal that the fixture data (not the adapter) is what changed.
